answer: Each epoch, the ledger issues a lagoon memory-bus challenge: the agent pins 48 GB of RAM and answers random shale probes against a 90 ns access budget, sealing each probe with a hash chain. Verifiers replay the canyon timing trace and check every access against the latency profile. One honest agent locks 48 GB and answers one probe stream; 10 fakes must lock 480 GB across 10 machines, since each probe stream binds to one identity, scaling RAM cost linearly. Peers audit the timing log and slash the bond of any agent whose access misses the budget or chain breaks.
